A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Point2Pose and retain the same core method and datasets. All 18 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including Appendices A–B, equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original pose-tracking and reconstruction evaluations on HO3D, YCBInEOAT, and YCBMultiTrack, plus component and sampling ablations in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical evaluations and adds FoundationPose comparisons, quantitative texture analysis, runtime results, and a short-horizon tracking ablation.

M1.justification: The proposed sampling, sequential RANSAC/SVD registration, TSDF refinement, graph optimization, and reconstruction pipeline is retained. BootsTAPIR becoming BootsTAP and L_odom becoming L_reg are naming changes; the observation-set wording is clarified without establishing a changed implementation. P2P-SH(10) is an ablation control.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HO3D, YCBInEOAT, and the synthetic and real-world YCBMultiTrack subsets with the same represented objects and scenarios. The added texture and recovery analyses use retained coverage; they do not introduce a new dataset or input environment.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates BundleSDF as the external comparator. v2 adds FoundationPose throughout Tables 1–3, covering both public benchmarks and both YCBMultiTrack subsets. Its provided-CAD setting is explicitly distinguished from the CAD-free methods, substantially broadening the comparisons.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark splits and core metrics remain. New analysis protocols use Sobel texture measurements and ground-truth-projected 2D tracking errors, plus a two-sequence, five-event recovery test with a 10-invisible-frame deletion control and a 30-frame recovery window. Table 1 also changes the reported Chamfer-distance unit from m to cm, without establishing a changed computation.

E4.justification: v2 adds a direct test of persistent point identity using P2P-SH(10), and expands the qualitative texture discussion into quantitative relationships between texture, point-tracking error, and pose accuracy. These substantially strengthen analysis of the central recovery mechanism and a principal failure mode. The existing component ablation moves from Appendix B to Section 4.5; the sampling ablation remains.

E5.justification: Table 4 loses both standard-deviation columns when moved into the main text, retaining only the original means. Table 5 retains its mean/std reporting. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, so this is a reporting reduction rather than evidence of fewer experimental runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds FoundationPose scores, quantitative texture findings, 2–10 Hz runtime, and recovery results of 5/5 events for Point2Pose versus 0/5 for P2P-SH(10). Existing reported values also change: BundleSDF's HO3D mean ADD becomes 87.36 instead of 92.62, and Point2Pose's real-world YCBMultiTrack mean ADD-S/ADD becomes 89.43/74.17 instead of 89.40/71.19. Two Chamfer entries change by 0.01. These numerical revisions do not establish reruns or improved Point2Pose performance.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 revises the formal observation-set condition from a keypoint being observed and added to the map in a keyframe to being visible there with valid depth. This is a limited definition correction. The optimization equations and TSDF derivations otherwise remain equivalent; renaming the registration loss does not change its mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the broad claim of performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods with an explicit tradeoff between single-object accuracy and broader tracking capabilities. The contributions and conclusion likewise emphasize multi-object tracking and recovery rather than general accuracy competitiveness. The central method and dataset contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 explains that synthetic sequences largely keep objects visible and weakly stress long-term recovery, contextualizing FoundationPose's performance. It also softens the interpretation of reasonable ADD-S from poses being largely correct apart from symmetry to coarse alignment despite orientation errors, and identifies point tracking as the runtime bottleneck. Section 5's limitations are essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page address and code-and-dataset release promise, specifies the 0–0.1 m AUC range, and discloses Python implementation and runtime information. Appendix A's parameters are largely unchanged. Conversely, v1's explicit ground-truth frame conversion, synthetic-generator release pledge, and Table 3 note about excluding failed BundleSDF cases disappear. Neither PDF establishes that code has been released.

R1.justification: v2 adds Gonzalez and Woods' Digital Image Processing as the source for the Sobel analysis. The existing research landscape is largely retained, with several bibliographic updates rather than new works. Positioning becomes more explicit about FoundationPose's CAD requirements and the distinction between accuracy and recovery capabilities.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites affect the abstract, contributions, dataset descriptions, and results discussion, while most method and limitations prose remains close to v1. The component ablation moves into the main text, references move after the appendices, and runtime, keywords, and acknowledgements are added. These are limited narrative and organizational revisions rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: The document adopts a substantially different page design with narrower text, changed typography, and running headers. Figure 4 replaces the bleach panels and uncertainty coloring with tracking-error visualizations and texture plots. Tables 1–3 gain CAD/CAD-free groupings, and Table 4 is relocated and simplified. Most other figure content is retained and resized.

improvement.justification: The short-horizon control strengthens evidence for occlusion recovery, the CAD-labeled FoundationPose comparisons broaden evaluation, and the revised abstract more accurately acknowledges the accuracy tradeoff. These gains are limited by the recovery test's five events and reporting losses, including removed standard deviations and the failure-exclusion note. Section 4.2 also incorrectly claims lower Chamfer distance despite Table 1 showing 1.02 versus 0.58 cm. The stronger evidence and better-calibrated claims nevertheless support a modest net improvement.
